modules.title: Stored Functions and Procedures
modules.goal: Put reusable logic in the database with the right volatility, security and transaction rules.

topics.title: Function vs Procedure
topics.simple: Function value return karta hai; procedure transaction control kar sakta hai.
topics.pro: Functions return a value and run inside the caller’s statement, while procedures are invoked with CALL and can manage transactions.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION student_count() RETURNS bigint LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students; $$;

topics.title: CREATE FUNCTION
topics.simple: CREATE FUNCTION named routine banata hai.
topics.pro: CREATE FUNCTION defines a routine with parameters, a return type, a language and a body.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION double_marks(p_marks integer) RETURNS integer LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT p_marks * 2; $$;

topics.title: RETURNS
topics.simple: RETURNS function ka output type batata hai.
topics.pro: The RETURNS clause declares a scalar, table, set or void result and must match what the body produces.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION student_name(p_id bigint) RETURNS text LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT name FROM students WHERE id = p_id; $$;

topics.title: SQL Functions
topics.simple: SQL function body plain SQL ho sakta hai.
topics.pro: A LANGUAGE sql function can contain SQL statements and is often inlined by the planner.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION high_scorers() RETURNS TABLE (id bigint, name text) LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT id, name FROM students WHERE marks >= 80; $$;

topics.title: PL/pgSQL Basics
topics.simple: PL/pgSQL procedural language hai.
topics.pro: PL/pgSQL adds variables, control flow, exceptions and multiple statements to database routines.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION grade_band(p_marks integer) RETURNS text LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN IF p_marks >= 90 THEN RETURN 'A'; ELSE RETURN 'B'; END IF; END; $$;

topics.title: Parameters
topics.simple: Function parameters input aur output ho sakte hain.
topics.pro: Parameters can be IN, OUT or INOUT; OUT parameters can define a result row without RETURNS TABLE.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION add_marks(p_id bigint, p_delta integer) RETURNS void LANGUAGE sql AS $$ UPDATE students SET marks = marks + p_delta WHERE id = p_id; $$;

topics.title: Returning Tables
topics.simple: RETURNS TABLE se multi-row result do.
topics.pro: RETURNS TABLE declares named output columns and lets the function return a set of rows.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION course_roster(p_course integer) RETURNS TABLE (student_id bigint, name text) LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT s.id, s.name FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id WHERE e.course_id = p_course; $$;

topics.title: CREATE PROCEDURE
topics.simple: Procedure CALL se chalti hai aur transaction control kar sakti hai.
topics.pro: CREATE PROCEDURE defines a routine invoked with CALL; procedures can commit or roll back inside their body.

example.sql: CREATE PROCEDURE archive_low_marks() LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN DELETE FROM students WHERE marks < 60; COMMIT; END; $$;

topics.title: CALL
topics.simple: CALL procedure ko invoke karta hai.
topics.pro: CALL executes a procedure with arguments and does not return a result set.

example.sql: CALL archive_low_marks();

topics.title: Transaction Control
topics.simple: Procedure ke andar COMMIT/ROLLBACK allowed hai.
topics.pro: Procedures can commit or roll back, but functions cannot; this is the key operational difference.

example.sql: CREATE PROCEDURE safe_archive() LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN DELETE FROM students WHERE marks < 60; COMMIT; END; $$;

topics.title: Exception Handling
topics.simple: PL/pgSQL EXCEPTION block errors pakadta hai.
topics.pro: An EXCEPTION block catches errors, lets you log or recover, and can re-raise with RAISE.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION safe_divide(a numeric, b numeric) RETURNS numeric LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN a / b; EXCEPTION WHEN division_by_zero THEN RETURN NULL; END; $$;

topics.title: SECURITY DEFINER
topics.simple: SECURITY DEFINER function owner ke privileges se chalta hai.
topics.pro: A SECURITY DEFINER function runs with the privileges of its owner, so it must lock down search_path and validate inputs.
points: Avoid dynamic SQL with untrusted input.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION admin_count() RETURNS bigint LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public AS $$ SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students; $$;

topics.title: Volatility
topics.simple: Volatility function ke side effects aur caching batati hai.
topics.pro: IMMUTABLE means same inputs always produce the same result, STABLE means constant within a statement, and VOLATILE can change or write.
points: VOLATILE is the default for writes.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION double_marks(p_marks integer) RETURNS integer LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$ SELECT p_marks * 2; $$;

topics.title: Function Overloading
topics.simple: Same name with different parameter types allowed hai.
topics.pro: PostgreSQL resolves overloaded functions by argument types, so ambiguous calls can fail.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION label(p_marks integer) RETURNS text LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT 'number'; $$;

topics.title: Dropping Routines
topics.simple: DROP FUNCTION/PROCEDURE routine hataata hai.
topics.pro: DROP FUNCTION or DROP PROCEDURE removes a routine; CASCADE also removes dependent objects.

example.sql: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS double_marks(integer);

topics.title: Common Routine Errors
topics.simple: Return mismatch, missing language aur transaction misuse common errors hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are a return type mismatch, a missing LANGUAGE clause, COMMIT inside a function and ambiguous overloads.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION bad() RETURNS integer LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT 'text'; $$;
example.output: ERROR: invalid input syntax for type integer

topics.title: Routine Performance
topics.simple: SQL functions inline; PL/pgSQL loops can be slow.
topics.pro: Simple SQL functions can be inlined and optimized, while procedural row-by-row loops often lose to set-based SQL.
points: Read the plan for function calls.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT double_marks(marks) FROM students;
example.output: A plan showing the function call.

topics.title: Testing Routines
topics.simple: Functions ko known inputs aur edge cases se test karo.
topics.pro: Test return values, NULL inputs, empty sets and error paths before relying on a routine in production.

example.sql: SELECT double_marks(NULL) AS doubled;

topics.title: Practical Function
topics.simple: Reusable validation ya calculation function banao.
topics.pro: A practical function keeps a single rule in one place and is marked with the correct volatility and security.

example.sql: CREATE FUNCTION is_passing(p_marks integer) RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$ SELECT COALESCE(p_marks >= 60, false); $$;

topics.title: Routine Maintenance
topics.simple: Routines ko version karo aur dependencies check karo.
topics.pro: Routine changes can break callers, so track signatures, test replacements and inspect dependencies before dropping.

example.sql: SELECT proname, pg_get_function_identity_arguments(oid) FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = 'double_marks';

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Function vs Procedure in a production query.
interview.answer: Functions return a value and run inside the caller’s statement, while procedures are invoked with CALL and can manage transactions. Key rules: Functions return values. Procedures use CALL. Procedures can COMMIT.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain CREATE FUNCTION in a production query.
interview.answer: CREATE FUNCTION defines a routine with parameters, a return type, a language and a body. Key rules: Name the function. Declare parameters. Choose the language.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain RETURNS in a production query.
interview.answer: The RETURNS clause declares a scalar, table, set or void result and must match what the body produces. Key rules: Use RETURNS TABLE for rows. Use SETOF for sets. RETURNS void means no value.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain SQL Functions in a production query.
interview.answer: A LANGUAGE sql function can contain SQL statements and is often inlined by the planner. Key rules: Simple and optimizable. Can return scalar or table. No procedural loops.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain PL/pgSQL Basics in a production query.
interview.answer: PL/pgSQL adds variables, control flow, exceptions and multiple statements to database routines. Key rules: Use BEGIN and END. Declare variables. Return explicitly.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Parameters in a production query.
interview.answer: Parameters can be IN, OUT or INOUT; OUT parameters can define a result row without RETURNS TABLE. Key rules: IN is the default. OUT adds a result column. Name parameters clearly.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Returning Tables in a production query.
interview.answer: RETURNS TABLE declares named output columns and lets the function return a set of rows. Key rules: Declare column names and types. Return a SELECT. Use it like a table.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain CREATE PROCEDURE in a production query.
interview.answer: CREATE PROCEDURE defines a routine invoked with CALL; procedures can commit or roll back inside their body. Key rules: Use CALL. Transaction control is allowed. No return value.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain CALL in a production query.
interview.answer: CALL executes a procedure with arguments and does not return a result set. Key rules: Use CALL, not SELECT. Arguments follow the name. It can manage transactions.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Transaction Control in a production query.
interview.answer: Procedures can commit or roll back, but functions cannot; this is the key operational difference. Key rules: Functions cannot COMMIT. Procedures can COMMIT. Be careful with partial success.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Exception Handling in a production query.
interview.answer: An EXCEPTION block catches errors, lets you log or recover, and can re-raise with RAISE. Key rules: Wrap risky statements. Use GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS. Re-raise when unsure.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain SECURITY DEFINER in a production query.
interview.answer: A SECURITY DEFINER function runs with the privileges of its owner, so it must lock down search_path and validate inputs. Key rules: It can grant controlled access. Set search_path explicitly. Avoid dynamic SQL with untrusted input.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Volatility in a production query.
interview.answer: IMMUTABLE means same inputs always produce the same result, STABLE means constant within a statement, and VOLATILE can change or write. Key rules: IMMUTABLE is strictest. STABLE reads the database. VOLATILE is the default for writes.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Function Overloading in a production query.
interview.answer: PostgreSQL resolves overloaded functions by argument types, so ambiguous calls can fail. Key rules: Overload by argument types. Avoid ambiguous defaults. Cast calls when needed.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Dropping Routines in a production query.
interview.answer: DROP FUNCTION or DROP PROCEDURE removes a routine; CASCADE also removes dependent objects. Key rules: Specify argument types. Use IF EXISTS in scripts. CASCADE is destructive.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Common Routine Errors in a production query.
interview.answer: Common failures are a return type mismatch, a missing LANGUAGE clause, COMMIT inside a function and ambiguous overloads. Key rules: Match RETURNS. Declare LANGUAGE. Use procedures for transactions.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Routine Performance in a production query.
interview.answer: Simple SQL functions can be inlined and optimized, while procedural row-by-row loops often lose to set-based SQL. Key rules: Prefer set-based SQL. Mark volatility correctly. Read the plan for function calls.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Testing Routines in a production query.
interview.answer: Test return values, NULL inputs, empty sets and error paths before relying on a routine in production. Key rules: Test NULL. Test empty input. Test error handling.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Practical Function in a production query.
interview.answer: A practical function keeps a single rule in one place and is marked with the correct volatility and security. Key rules: Name it clearly. Type the parameters. Document the contract.

interview.q: Module 24 · Explain Routine Maintenance in a production query.
interview.answer: Routine changes can break callers, so track signatures, test replacements and inspect dependencies before dropping. Key rules: Track signatures. Use CREATE OR REPLACE carefully. Check pg_depend.

Parameters can be IN, OUT or INOUT; OUT parameters can define a result row without RETURNS TABLE. IN is the default. OUT adds a result column. Name parameters clearly.

logic.q: Module 24 · Why does Returning Tables matter?
logic.answer: RETURNS TABLE declares named output columns and lets the function return a set of rows. Declare column names and types. Return a SELECT. Use it like a table.

logic.q: Module 24 · Why does CREATE PROCEDURE matter?
logic.answer: CREATE PROCEDURE defines a routine invoked with CALL; procedures can commit or roll back inside their body. Use CALL. Transaction control is allowed. No return value.
CALL executes a procedure with arguments and does not return a result set. Use CALL, not SELECT. Arguments follow the name. It can manage transactions.

logic.q: Module 24 · Why does Transaction Control matter?
logic.answer: Procedures can commit or roll back, but functions cannot; this is the key operational difference. Functions cannot COMMIT. Procedures can COMMIT. Be careful with partial success.

logic.q: Module 24 · Why does Exception Handling matter?
logic.answer: An EXCEPTION block catches errors, lets you log or recover, and can re-raise with RAISE. Wrap risky statements. Use GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS. Re-raise when unsure.

logic.q: Module 24 · Why does SECURITY DEFINER matter?
logic.answer: A SECURITY DEFINER function runs with the privileges of its owner, so it must lock down search_path and validate inputs. It can grant controlled access. Set search_path explicitly. Avoid dynamic SQL with untrusted input.

IMMUTABLE means same inputs always produce the same result, STABLE means constant within a statement, and VOLATILE can change or write. IMMUTABLE is strictest. STABLE reads the database. VOLATILE is the default for writes.

logic.q: Module 24 · Why does Function Overloading matter?
logic.answer: PostgreSQL resolves overloaded functions by argument types, so ambiguous calls can fail. Overload by argument types. Avoid ambiguous defaults. Cast calls when needed.

logic.q: Module 24 · Why does Dropping Routines matter?
logic.answer: DROP FUNCTION or DROP PROCEDURE removes a routine; CASCADE also removes dependent objects. Specify argument types. Use IF EXISTS in scripts. CASCADE is destructive.

debug.title: Missing language
debug.broken: CREATE FUNCTION double_marks(p integer) RETURNS integer AS $$ SELECT p * 2; $$;
debug.fix: CREATE FUNCTION double_marks(p integer) RETURNS integer LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT p * 2; $$;

debug.title: Return mismatch
debug.broken: CREATE FUNCTION bad() RETURNS integer LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT 'text'; $$;
debug.fix: CREATE FUNCTION bad() RETURNS text LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT 'text'; $$;
debug.error: invalid input syntax for type integer

debug.title: COMMIT in function
debug.broken: CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN COMMIT; END; $$;
debug.fix: CREATE PROCEDURE p() LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN COMMIT; END; $$;
debug.error: COMMIT is not allowed in a function

debug.title: Ambiguous overload
Search path risk
debug.broken: CREATE FUNCTION admin_count() RETURNS bigint LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER AS $$ SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students; $$;
debug.fix: CREATE FUNCTION admin_count() RETURNS bigint LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public AS $$ SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students; $$;
debug.error: A caller-controlled search_path can hijack names

debug.title: Volatility lie
debug.broken: CREATE FUNCTION now_text() RETURNS text LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$ SELECT NOW()::text; $$;
debug.fix: CREATE FUNCTION now_text() RETURNS text LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$ SELECT NOW()::text; $$;
debug.error: An IMMUTABLE function must not change over time

debug.title: Exception swallowed
debug.broken: CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN INSERT INTO missing_table VALUES (1); EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL; END; $$;
debug.fix: CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN INSERT INTO missing_table VALUES (1); EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN RAISE; END; $$;
